title: Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS)

location: Georgia Tech, Atlanta · Virtual participation possible
cost: NeurIPS registration is not required; workshop fees not verified.
effort: Up to four pages plus references; technical contribution or thoughtful research perspective.
lifecycleEvidence: 2026 submission deadline and workshop date are announced on the organizer's page.

title: Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
description: A NeurIPS workshop accepting short papers, proposals, and tutorial notebooks with a credible path to climate impact. Submissions are non-archival: workshop presentation is not a proceedings publication. The 2026 submission window has closed.
eligibility: Interdisciplinary researchers; no school-year restriction stated in the inspected call. Advanced students should confirm author and minor-attendance requirements; a mentor can help establish a meaningful climate application.
cost: Check conference registration and travel costs; no funding guarantee.
effort: Anonymized submission via OpenReview; demonstrate climate relevance and follow track-specific guidelines.
lifecycleEvidence: Submission deadline passed. Workshop listed as December 11/12, 2026; exact day remains ambiguous and is not converted into a single date.

title: Machine Learning for Health (ML4H)
description: Now a standalone symposium, formerly a NeurIPS-affiliated workshop. Offers an eight-page archival Proceedings track and a four-page non-archival Findings track for preliminary insights, datasets, reproducibility, and negative results.
eligibility: Research-level work with health relevance; no school-year restriction stated in the inspected call. Advanced students should confirm eligibility and minor attendance. Required human-subject/IRB approvals must be addressed.
cost: Confirm symposium registration and travel costs; grants are not guaranteed.
effort: Double-blind review; choose archival Proceedings or non-archival Findings carefully. OpenReview account required.
lifecycleEvidence: ML4H has transitioned from a NeurIPS-affiliated workshop into a standalone symposium. Current paper deadline is September 10, 2026.
